Briskham Manor — 7554 Briskham Street

Confirmed apartment-form. 33 units in the development, Strata Plan LMS1049. Construction: frame wood with brick exterior and vinyl siding, 3 storeys. Gas and hot water are included in the strata fees per listings, and parking is secure under-building. The sheet shows zoning MA1.
Mission Manor — 33165 2nd Avenue
Built 1992. The directory records restrictions as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed.
Glenkirk Court — 7436 Stave Lake Street
Built 1975, 38 units. Listings note shared laundry, and one current listing states "No short term rentals" for the building.
Montgomery Condos — developer address 7375 Horne Street

(resale listings also address units at 33281 2 Avenue). Six storeys, 85 units, by Redekop Faye, with estimated completion in 2026 (developer source) — a presale/just-completed building, so REDMA applied to developer contracts. The presale record describes a 4-storey woodframe building of 103 condominiums plus 11 affordable rental units, and states condo rentals were permitted for 100 years under the project's housing agreement (presale source). Amenities in listings: clubhouse, exercise centre, yoga/games and co-working rooms, dog wash.

Named in one current listing.

items.t: Mission replaced its OCP in 2026. Bylaw 6405-2026 was adopted June 1, 2026, replacing Bylaw 6350-2025 — planning documents and listing copy citing the old OCP are already a bylaw out of date. The City states the new bylaw is substantively the same OCP, with a Regional Context Statement formally incorporated.

Montgomery carries two addresses. The developer markets 7375 Horne Street while resale listings address units at 33281 2 Avenue — the same building. Confirm which address a specific unit's title and strata records use before ordering documents.

Luther Place also carries two addresses — 7525 Martin Place in listings, 32286 7th Avenue in the building directory — and its units surface in "condo" feeds even though the MLS dwelling type is Townhouse. Both facts will confuse a buyer's document search if not pointed out first.

Central amenities a condo buyer actually uses: Mission Leisure Centre at 7650 Grand Street and Mission Memorial Hospital at 7324 Hurd Street anchor the central core the condo buildings cluster around.

items.t: The real estate board divides Mission into nine areas: Dewdney Deroche, Durieu, Hatzic, Hemlock, Lake Errock, Mission, Mission West, Stave Falls and Steelhead. The core "Mission" area has most of the homes for sale.
Municipal geography: the City of Mission in the Fraser Valley, east of Maple Ridge and north of Abbotsford across the Fraser River.

Where the condos and townhomes are, September 2026 (listed / sold): Mission 104 / 10; Hemlock 9 / 0; Mission West 8 / 0; Lake Errock 1 / 0; all others none. Every condo and townhome sale that month was in the core Mission area.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the urban core and Mission West — Cherry Lane and Luther Place on/near Seventh Avenue, Briskham Hill on Briskham Street west of downtown, and Archer Green on Nelson Street in Mission West.
A feed claim checked and not carried: a first-page listing card names a "Mission Elementary School" near 4th Avenue.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Mission BC

items.t: For the strata complexes, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. It matters most for Mission's oldest townhouses (Luther Place, 1988; Cherry Lane, 1989).

Secondary suites: in Mission, all suites must be registered with the City. A suite is a self-contained unit inside a single detached house, on the same title, and isn't allowed in townhouses or rowhomes. The registration period closed May 16, 2024, so a new suite now needs a building permit, and the City can investigate an unregistered suite and may require a permit to remove it.

City property taxes: Mission's 2026 taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a flat 10% penalty added on July 3 to any unpaid balance (including unclaimed home owner grants). That's the whole penalty. The two-step 5% + 5% schedule (after July 2 and October 31) is the rural system for regional district areas outside the City, not the City's.

ALR (rural edges): Mission's rural sub-areas include farm land; on ALR parcels the ALC frame is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha), and ALR residences cannot be stratified.

Flood and dykes: the Fraser River floodplain runs along the city's south edge and Hatzic Prairie sits behind the Dewdney Dyke system; Mission taxes also carry a diking levy. Flood status and insurance terms are parcel- and building-specific — check both.

items.t: Two of Mission's four townhouse complexes predate 1990 — and both are 55+.

Mission's tax penalty is a single step, unlike its neighbours'. One flat 10% on July 3, 2026 for unpaid 2026 balances — Surrey's two-step 5% + 5% and the FVRD rural 5% + 5% are different regimes that do not apply inside the City.
The train is a weekday-only asset. Five trains each way, 75 minutes, no weekends or statutory holidays — a Mission townhouse marketed on the commute delivers that asset Monday to Friday only.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Mission BC

items.t: Official Community Plan: Mission's OCP Bylaw 6405-2026 was adopted June 1, 2026, after a public hearing on April 7, 2026, replacing Bylaw 6350-2025. The City says it's essentially the same plan, with the same vision, land use, maps and policies, redone to fix a procedural issue and add a Regional Context Statement required by provincial law.

Zoning: City of Mission Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020: (cited in the City's own amending bylaws as "District of Mission Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020"). Parcel zone, minimum lot area and permitted uses are read from the consolidated bylaw per parcel.

SSMUH / added units (Mission frame): the City incorporated the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing legislation into Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020 on July 17, 2024 (Bylaw 6299-2024-5949(163)); as part of that amendment the Urban Residential 930 Secondary Dwelling Zone (R930s) was removed and merged with R930. Added-unit permission is not permission to subdivide.

Secondary suites: in Mission, all suites must be registered with the City. A suite is a self-contained unit inside a single detached house, on the same title, and isn't allowed in townhouses or rowhomes. A new suite needs a building permit, and an unregistered suite can lead to a bylaw investigation and a required removal permit.

Development charges (context for a subdivision/build): the City's Development Cost Charge Bylaw 6348-2025 was adopted May 5, 2025, and DCCs apply to every person who obtains approval of a subdivision (among other triggers); the Amenity Cost Charge Bylaw 6349-2025 was adopted the same day, payable at subdivision approval or building permit issuance. Amounts are in the bylaws.

On ALR land: subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and one additional home can be up to 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger).

Mission property taxes are due July 2, with a flat 10% penalty added on July 3 to any unpaid balance (including unclaimed home owner grants). That's different from Surrey's two-step 5% + 5% and from the regional district's rural 5% + 5% schedule.

Floodplain / hazard diligence: Parcel-level hazard, riparian and geotechnical items are read from the City's site-assessment process under DSCB 5650-2017 (Schedule J asks, among other things, about septic systems, ditching/ponds and vegetation) per application.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mission BC lots

items.t: The OCP bylaw changed numbers without changing the plan. Bylaw 6405-2026 (adopted June 1, 2026) replaced 6350-2025 with, in the City's own words, substantively the same OCP plus a Regional Context Statement, to address a procedural matter in the 2025 adoption. A designation cited from either bylaw should be checked against the in-force bylaw before it is priced.
Mission's tax penalty is one step, not two. A flat 10% on July 3 — cross-city comparisons that import Surrey's 5% + 5% or the FVRD rural 5% + 5% misstate a Mission completion adjustment.

A detached house can sit on a strata lot in Mission. Heritage Park Place cards describe detached ranchers inside a strata subdivision — form and tenure are different questions, and a "detached" card is not proof of fee-simple title.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Mission BC
What a duplex looks like in Mission BC

items.t: The usual duplex form: The ordinary Mission duplex form is the individual duplex building on a single lot built under the zoning of its day, sold whole unless it was strata-divided into a 2-lot plan or subdivided fee-simple. The City's own SSMUH framing confirms duplex dwellings are a recognised baseline form in Mission: Zones previously restricted to single family or duplex dwellings are subject to the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing legislation the City has adopted.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Mission BC

items.t: OCP: City of Mission Official Community Plan Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, replacing and repealing OCP Bylaw 6350-2025 and keeping the same vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction, with a Regional Context Statement added; the bylaw was put to a public hearing on April 7, 2026.

SSMUH: The City incorporated the provincial small-scale multi-unit housing legislation into Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020 on July 17, 2024 (Bylaw 6299-2024); as part of that amendment the Urban Residential 930 Secondary Dwelling Zone (R930s) was removed and merged with R930. The City states zones previously restricted to single-family or duplex dwellings as of December 7, 2023 are subject to the legislation, subject to eligibility and servicing. Added-unit permission is not permission to subdivide.

Secondary suites (Mission's own rule): All secondary suites in Mission must be registered with the City; a secondary suite is a self-contained living space in a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity, suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes, and adding one goes through the building permit process. City" is a claim to verify against the City, not a fact.
Servicing / subdivision: A fee-simple split of a duplex parcel runs through this City process against the zone minimums in Bylaw 5949-2020.
